newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Italy EMU entry delay would not be trauma.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Italy EMU entry delay would not be trauma.

text.p: A delay in Italy's entry into European economic and monetary union (EMU) beyond the planned launch date of 1999 would not have a negative impact on Italian financial markets, a Reuter poll of economists showed.

The survey of 10 Italian analysts conducted after the Financial Times reported on Wednesday that Italy will be offered a deal delaying its entry until 2000 or 2001 also showed a majority believed Italian EMU entry would be postponed.

Nearly half those polled believe a decision on the timing of Italian EMU entry would be taken in the course of 1997. The remainder thought a decision would be put off until the spring of 1998, as foreseen under the Maastricht Treaty.
Most analysts surveyed do not see a delay having a negative impact.
The consensus view is that the market by year end will show an improvement in its performance.

The spread between 10-year Italian treasury bonds (Btps) and 10-year Bunds is seen narrowing to 125 basis points from 155 at present while the discount rate is expected to fall to 5.75 percent from 6.75 percent.
The lira/mark rate is expected to weaken to 990 lire, from 985 at present, in line with its central ERM parity rate.
Lorenzo Codogno, chief economist at Bank of America in Milan said he believes a clear signal will come in the next few months as to who will be among the first to join EMU.
"I remain pessimistic over the chances of Italy being in EMU from the beginning even if, paradoxically, the Financial Times helps Prodi who now has more strength to ask for sacrifices," said Codogno.

Cariplo's Renzo Avesani said he expected a decision on the EMU ins and outs in the coming months. "The die will be cast by the end of the first half of 1997 and it is very probable that Italy and Spain will start one year late."
However, San Paolo's Francesco Giordano said he believed a decision would be postponed until next year. "A decision will only be reached in 1998, when all the 1997 numbers are on the table," he said.
Survey results (10 analysts polled):
Question one - A decision on the timing of Italy's entry into EMU will be decided in 1997 or 1998?
Answer -- In 1997 (four replies); in 1998 (five replies); don't know (one reply).
Question two -- Will Italy be admitted to the first group of EMU members?
Answer -- Yes (three replies); No (seven replies); don't know (none).
Market forecasts for end 1997:
10-year BTP/Bund spread -- Consensus 125 basis points, maximum 180 bps, minimum 95 bps.
Mark/lira exchange rate -- Consensus 990 lire, maximum 1,000 lire, minimum 980 lire.
Bank of Italy discount rate -- Consensus 5.75 percent, maximum 6.25 percent, minimum 5.00 percent.
Analyst from the following organisations took part in the poll -- Bank of America, Banco di Sardegna, Banque Indosuez, Caboto, Cariplo, Centrosim, Credito Italiano, JP Morgan, Natwest, San Paolo.
